report.source_text: The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy, which revealed significant adherences between the sigmoid colon and the urinary bladder (Figure 3 a). The sigmoid colon was carefully separated from the posterior wall of the urinary bladder. Along the connection, necrotic tissue was also evident along with multiple diverticula (Figure 3 b). A recto-sigmoidectomy of approximately 15 cm was done along with a proximal segment colostomy.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old patient presented with a 3-month history of dysuria, fecaluria, pneumaturia, and abdominal pain, with prior episodes of cystitis that failed antibiotic therapy from a general practitioner. On admission, the patient was vitally stable (E001). Laboratory investigation revealed elevated WBC (11.360), hemoglobin 12.4, raised urea (74 mg/dL), and raised creatinine (2.5 mg/dL) (E002), indicating systemic inflammation and renal involvement. Ultrasound imaging identified a 1.5 cm defect between the sigmoid colon and urinary bladder with passage of echogenic material into the bladder, distinguishable from normal ureteric jets (E004), directly confirming an entero-vesical fistula. The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy, which revealed significant adherences between the sigmoid colon and posterior bladder wall, with necrotic tissue and multiple diverticula along the connection (E006). A recto-sigmoidectomy of approximately 15 cm was performed with proximal segment colostomy (E006), confirming both the fistula and diverticulosis as the underlying etiology.

Exploratory laparotomy confirmed the diagnosis by revealing significant adherences between sigmoid colon and bladder, necrotic tissue, and multiple diverticula
